newsitem.title: GERMANY: German industrial oilseeds area down at 115,000 ha.
newsitem.headline: German industrial oilseeds area down at 115,000 ha.

text.p: German farmers have applied to grow oilseeds for industrial uses on set-aside land totalling 115,000 hectares in 1997, state intervention board BLE said.
BLE, which collects the applications, said this was down from 240,000 ha in 1996 and mostly reflected the halving of the set-aside rate to five percent.
Under European Union farm rules, farmers may grow industrial crops while still being able to collect compensation for set-aside, which aims at balancing food supply and prices.

So-called "00"-rapeseed accounted for just under 100,000 ha of the 1997 total, down from 230,000 ha in 1996. As this type is identical with food rapeseed, its mandatory sales to industry for non-food consumption are strictly monitored and violations carry penalties.
Eruca rapeseed, with a 40 percent share of non-edible acids, accounted for 10,100 ha after 4,000 ha in 1996.
BLE reported major expansions in the eastern German states of Brandenburg, Saxony-Anhalt and Saxony.

The area for industrial linseed dropped to 700 ha from 1,350 ha last year. BLE said linseed had become unpopular after prices of linseed oil in technical applications had dropped and farmers were unable to crush and sell linseed meal instead as this would have constituted a food use.
The remainder of the total in both years was made up of minor crops.
Major non-food uses declared were biofuels, hydraulic and technical oils, BLE said.
